title: Prescriptions Desk System Card: Declining an Owed Balance on a Non-Controlled Prescription
content:
A patient may decline the open owed balance of a Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Non-Controlled Acute Prescription, Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription or Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription class — the units still owed after a short fill — and receive the non-controlled decline credit for them.

## Governing rule

- The balance itself is cancelled for its full owed units exactly as the Prescriptions owed-balance rules provide, and the credit is recorded on the cancellation entry.
- A short fill's patient pay covers the full prescribed quantity, so the part of it that paid for units never dispensed is credited when the patient declines them. The credit is the non-controlled decline credit, returned by the original payment method.
- Apart from this credit, a fill of these classes that was dispensed correctly is never taken back or refunded, whatever the reason the patient gives.

## Capability of the tool

`decline_owed_balance_20c85924` lets the patient decline, in person, the units Kestrel still owes on a prescription dispensed short, and take back the credit for them. One call cancels the named owed balance for its full owed units: it books a balance cancellation entry on the prescription's fill ledger that names the owed-balance entry, records today's date, the units cancelled and the credit returned to the patient, and lowers the prescription's owed quantity by those units. The cancelled units are never dispensed afterwards. After the call the patient sees the balance as cancelled and the credit amount on the cancellation entry, and the owed-balance entry is no longer open.

## How it is invoked

This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the patient — then runs it (through `call_user_discoverable_tool`).

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `source_fill_id` | the reference number of the owed-balance entry being declined, as the agent reads it from the prescription's fill ledger and tells the patient | text identifier |
| `refund_usd` | the credit returned to the patient for the declined units, as the agent states it | USD with 2 decimal places, a positive amount rounded to the cent |

## Return

A text rendering of a dictionary describing the cancellation:

- `cancellation_id` — text, the new fill-ledger reference;
- `source_fill_id` — text, the owed-balance entry cancelled;
- `owed_units_cancelled` — integer dosage units no longer owed;
- `refund_usd` — number, USD with 2 decimal places credited;
- `owed_quantity_after` — integer units still owed on the prescription;
- `status` — text, "balance_declined" when the entry was written.

## Illustration (hypothetical input)

With a `source_fill_id` naming an owed-balance entry of 10 units and a `refund_usd` of 8.00, the return shows `owed_units_cancelled` 10, `refund_usd` 8.0, the units still owed afterwards in `owed_quantity_after`, and the status "balance_declined".
